claim: BOOST (Park & Cheon et al.) jointly selects a Gaussian-process kernel (Matern, RBF, or Rational Quadratic) and an acquisition function (EI, PI, LCB, or Posterior Mean) at each iteration of a standard online Bayesian optimization loop, making it the closest identified near-miss to a crossed surrogate x optimizer selection scheme in the BO/AutoML literature.
stance_target: N6 near-miss inventory: kernel x acquisition-function joint selection in Bayesian optimization
scope_conditions: online Bayesian optimization, synthetic benchmarks and ML hyperparameter tuning tasks, 2025-2026
quoted_support: BOOST: A Data-Driven Framework for the Automated Joint Selection of Kernel and Acquisition Functions in Bayesian Optimization.

claim: All three kernels compared in BOOST (Matern, RBF, Rational Quadratic) are covariance functions for a single Gaussian Process surrogate model class, not distinct model architectures (e.g. GP vs neural network vs random forest), so the paper's kernel variation does not satisfy a surrogate-model-CLASS crossing requirement.
stance_target: BOOST as a candidate KILL of N6
quoted_support: The kernel functions considered in this work are defined as follows: k_Matern(r), k_RBF(r), k_RQ(r) ... The Matern kernel offers tunable smoothness, the Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel assumes infinite differentiability, and the Rational Quadratic (RQ) kernel accommodates multiple characteristic length scales.

claim: BOOST's 'offline evaluation' terminology refers to a no-extra-query meta-selection subroutine run inside an otherwise fully online Bayesian optimization loop with live oracle queries every iteration, not to offline model-based optimization over a fixed static dataset.
stance_target: BOOST operates in the offline/fixed-dataset MBO setting required for an N6 kill
quoted_support: BOOST utilizes a simple offline evaluation stage to predict the performance of ... BOOST performs offline evaluation using previously observed points

claim: BOOST includes an ablation (Appendix C.5, 'Effect of fixing the kernel function or acquisition function') that isolates the individual contribution of the kernel axis versus the acquisition-function axis, which is the closest approach to a two-factor ablation found across all three searched regions -- but it lacks a genuine cross-model-class factor and a formal variance decomposition (ANOVA/eta-squared).
stance_target: closest structural near-miss to N6's crossed-factorial requirement
quoted_support: C.5 Effect of fixing the kernel function or acquisition function
